replies.author: @edinsoncode
replies.reply_text: "Can I undo what it did" is the test most tools fail quietly. Cheapest fix: start every agent run on its own branch or git worktree, so undo is one delete. CodeTruss is also worth a look; it checks the agent stayed in scope before you accept the change.

replies.author: @spencerldixon
replies.reply_text: From the plugin side: non-devs mostly want the boring chores done. Sendpaper mails real postcards, PostEverywhere schedules social posts, DamnPDFs handles PDF/Office grunt work. We track 344 Codex/ChatGPT plugins at pickaplugin.com and the non-code ones say a lot.

replies.author: @VarunChopr17597
replies.reply_text: Mine would be a red-green test loop: the agent has to write a failing test that reproduces the bug before it's allowed to touch the fix. Kills the "fixed it!" that fixed nothing. Red-Green Proof packages exactly that for Codex and Claude Code.

replies.author: @MagnusOlseq8r6
replies.reply_text: 48 is wild but not surprising: each open Claude Code or Codex session starts its own copy of every local (stdio) MCP server. Closing sessions you're done with helps, and for servers you use everywhere, a remote/HTTP version means one process instead of dozens.

replies.author: @liran_tal
replies.reply_text: A Go binary can't run inside a Worker itself, but Cloudflare Containers can run it: package it as a Docker image and have a Worker route the HTTP traffic to it. For the missing auth, Cloudflare's workers-oauth-provider library can sit in that Worker in front of it.

replies.author: @RoundtableSpace
replies.reply_text: Sandboxing fixes what the agent can read. The leak that bites more often is the agent pasting a secret into a prompt, a log or a commit. Pair the sandbox with a hook layer: Agent Guard blocks or masks secrets in Claude Code and Codex, locally, with no telemetry.

replies.author: @marcinperlak
replies.reply_text: Good catch. Rules tied to one tool hold up better inside that tool's own description, right where the agent decides whether to call it. Keep those short too, since some clients clip tool descriptions as well. Server-wide instructions are for the few rules that apply everywhere.

replies.author: @constance_etin
replies.reply_text: Spec-to-MCP is the right starting point. The step people skip is pruning: a big API mapped 1:1 into 80 tools buries the agent in choices. Folding the handful of calls people actually make into a few task-shaped tools usually beats exposing every endpoint.
